# London Spare-Room Rental Checklist for a 6-Month Let

A practical, tenant-friendly checklist for renting one room in a 2-bedroom flat in London from **2026-09-01** for **6 months**. This is a process guide, not legal advice.

## Step-by-Step Rental Setup

- Confirm the letting model: **lodger/room let** versus a full tenancy, based on how the owner will live in the flat and how access/shared use will work.
- Check building and mortgage/lease constraints before advertising: landlord consent, leaseholder restrictions, building rules, and insurance requirements.
- Make the room ready: safe locks, working smoke/CO alarms, clean condition, furniture list, and clear access to kitchen/bathroom/shared areas.
- Decide the rent structure: monthly rent, deposit amount, bills included or excluded, payment date, and any late-payment process.
- Prepare a short written agreement covering the 6-month fixed term, notice expectations, house rules, privacy, and maintenance responsibilities.
- Use a fair, consistent screening process for every applicant.
- Keep records of adverts, messages, viewings, references, and decisions.

## Documents, Checks, and Viewing Questions

| Stage | What to prepare | What to ask or verify | Common mistake to avoid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before advertising | Room description, photos, rent, bills, deposit, move-in date, agreement draft | Is the room suitable for one person only? What occupancy limit applies? | Vague listing that later causes disputes |
| Fair screening | Same application form for all candidates | Employment, income, right to rent, references, move-in date, lifestyle fit | Asking inconsistent questions or making decisions on irrelevant personal traits |
| Viewing | Printed key facts sheet | Work pattern, guests, smoking, cleanliness expectations, noise tolerance, remote work needs | Overselling privacy or understating shared-space access |
| Offer stage | Written summary of terms | Can the tenant meet the rent and deposit? Do they understand the 6-month term? | Agreeing terms verbally only |
| Move-in | Inventory, meter readings, check-in photos, keys log | Does the tenant accept the condition report and house rules? | Skipping the inventory and deposit record |
| During the let | Maintenance log, contact details, notice process | Any repair issues, safety concerns, or changes in circumstances? | Delaying repairs or entering the room without notice |

## Fair Screening and Viewing Questions

- “What is your ideal move-in date, and do you need the room for the full 6 months?”
- “What does a typical weekday look like for you: office, hybrid, or remote work?”
- “Do you expect to work from home regularly, and would you need quiet hours?”
- “How often do you have guests, and would overnight guests be an issue?”
- “Do you smoke or vape?”
- “Do you have any pets, or would you expect to bring one?”
- “How do you usually handle shared-space cleaning and cooking?”
- “Can you provide references from a landlord, employer, or current housemate?”
- “Are there any access needs or lifestyle requirements we should plan for?”
- “Are you comfortable with the house rules on noise, guests, and shared areas?”

## House Rules and Privacy Protections

- Set quiet hours, especially for work nights and early mornings.
- Define guest rules: daytime visitors, overnight stays, and advance notice.
- Clarify shared-space use: kitchen storage, bathroom timing, laundry, and cleaning rota.
- State whether the owner can enter the room, and under what notice or emergency conditions.
- Keep the tenant’s room private: no routine entry, no moving belongings, no shared access without permission.
- Separate personal and tenant storage areas clearly.
- Agree how post, parcels, and deliveries will be handled.
- Include a respectful process for complaints, repairs, and housemate conflicts.

## Safety, Condition, and Maintenance Checks

- Test smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms before move-in.
- Check locks, windows, lighting, heating, and hot water.
- Fix damp, mould, leaks, trip hazards, and electrical issues before advertising.
- Provide basic furniture only if it is in safe condition.
- Take dated photos of the room and shared areas at move-in.
- Record meter readings if bills are separate.
- Keep a simple repair log with date, issue, action, and completion.

## Money and Paperwork to Keep

- Signed room agreement or lodger agreement
- Deposit receipt and deposit terms
- Inventory and check-in photos
- Copy of tenant ID and right-to-rent evidence, if applicable to the arrangement
- Reference checks and contact details
- Rent schedule and payment record
- House rules sheet signed or acknowledged
- Repair and maintenance log
- Notice correspondence and any agreed changes in writing

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

- Using different screening criteria for different applicants.
- Ignoring lease, mortgage, or insurer restrictions.
- Forgetting to document the room condition at move-in.
- Mixing up bills, deposit, and rent in informal messages.
- Overpromising privacy when the owner still needs occasional access to shared areas.
- Failing to address damp, mould, or safety issues before the tenant moves in.
- Relying on verbal agreements for key terms like guests, notice, or repairs.
- Letting the room to more than one occupant if the setup is intended for one person only.
